text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Bulgaria's main opposition presidential candidate Petar Stoyanov and Socialist candidate Ivan Marazov face a run-off on November 3 after they won 44-45 and 25.5-28 percent of the votes respectively in the first round on Sunday according to preliminary projections.
-- A Bulgarian trade delegation is leaving for Moscow to negotiate cuts in import duties for Bulgarian goods, deputy trade minister Vladimir Karpachev said.
-- Bulgaria's central bank and the State Savings Bank have extended over 100 billion levs in refinancing to local commercial banks during the first six months of the year, central bank data shows.
Commercial banks have extended 875 billion levs credits for the same period with only 50.14 percent of which have been serviced regularly.
-- No major irregularities were reported during Sunday's presidential elections, said a Central Electoral Committee's spokeswoman. Turnout was estimated at 55-60 percent.

-- Raiffeisen Bulgaria is negotiating with the government for the purchase of the Varna-based state-owned Expressbank, a Reiffeisenzentral official said. Reiffeisen Bulgaria is expected to post a zero profit for 1996, the official added.
-- The national carrier Balkan Airlines on Sunday closed loss-makimg destinations to Madrid, Barcelona, Munich and Helsinki. There will be one flight a week to Stockholm, Balkan officials said.

-- Bulgaria's montly inflation was projected around 15 percent in October and cumulative inflation for the first ten months of the year was expected near 190 percent, experts said. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
